PullRequest.Title: Mobile chat (1/10): infra primitives — bottom sheet body, visualViewport, longPress, pulldown, edge-swipe
PullRequest.Body:
**Part 1 of 10** in the mobile-chat work split. This PR ships the foundation primitives the rest of the stack depends on. See plan in #TBD (issue).

### Scope

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `mobilePickerSheet.ts` + `.css` | Extract shared sheet shell into `buildMobileSheetShell` helper; export new `showMobileContentSheet(container, title, renderBody, options?)` for arbitrary-body bottom sheets. `showMobilePickerSheet` signature unchanged. |
| `mobileVisualViewport.ts` (new) | `IMobileVisualViewport` service: `keyboardHeight` observable + writes `--vscode-keyboard-height` CSS variable + sets `KeyboardVisibleContext` (>50px threshold). Replaces the inline `visualViewport` block previously in `workbench.ts`. |
| `longPress.ts` (new) | Reusable `installLongPress(el, handler, opts?)` helper — pointer-based hold detection with movement-threshold cancellation, optional `layoutService` phone-gating, synthetic-click suppression. |
| `mobilePulldownDismiss.ts` (new) | `installPulldownDismiss(overlay, header, onDismiss)` — vertical pointer-drag dismissal with snap-back below threshold. |
| `mobileEdgeSwipe.ts` (new) | `installMobileEdgeSwipeToOpenSidebar(container, openSidebar, layoutService)` — left-edge swipe gesture. |
| `vscode-known-variables.json` | Register `--vscode-keyboard-height` for stylelint. |
| `workbench.ts` | Wire `IMobileVisualViewport` (resolves the singleton during startup). |

### Why split

No new UI yet — just primitives. Every follow-up PR (#2-#8) imports from these files. Landing this alone keeps the diff reviewable and unblocks 7 parallel follow-up PRs.

### Validation

- ✅ `npm run compile-check-ts-native`
- ✅ `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Hygiene: only pre-existing errors in the new `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features` bundled extension (unrelated to this branch).

### Follow-ups (draft PRs queued)

2. iOS keyboard avoidance (uses `IMobileVisualViewport`)
3. Mobile overlays + code-block (uses `showMobileContentSheet` + `installPulldownDismiss` + `installMobileEdgeSwipeToOpenSidebar`)
4. Tool confirmation + plan review bottom sheets
5. Chat row long-press actions (uses `installLongPress`)
6. Inline diff routing + inline anchor peek
7. Running-chat chip lanes + streaming FAB
8. Context-add + completion sheet + voice dictation
9. Mobile titlebar overflow menu (independent of #1)
10. Content-parts CSS sweep + MOBILE.md (independent of #1)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The Promise executor invokes the caller-controlled renderer synchronously after buildMobileSheetShell has appended the overlay and registered window/visualViewport listeners. JavaScript converts a renderer throw into a rejected promise, but no code reaches shell.close or disposables.dispose, and the function returns no other handle. The only uncertainty is how often a renderer fails; the leak mechanism and per-failure growth are direct.
Findings.PerformanceResource: mounted overlay DOM nodes, Gesture targets, window keydown listener, visualViewport resize/scroll listeners, and any body DOM appended before the throw
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each failed invocation retains one additional sheet subtree and three global event listeners indefinitely; later viewport and key events fan out across all leaked shells.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: unbounded retained memory and increasing UI-event CPU work after repeated failed sheet opens
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no arbitrary-body content-sheet renderer path, so a caller renderer could not fail after this helper mounted a shell and strand its cleanup store.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new content-sheet path builds and mounts the shell, then directly invokes renderBody inside the Promise executor without failure cleanup; a synchronous throw rejects the promise while leaving the shell live in the document.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 425 invokes the new caller-controlled renderBody after lines 413-420 create the mounted shell, with no try/finally or rejection cleanup around the call.
Findings.Title: Dispose the sheet shell when body rendering throws
Findings.Impact: If a sheet body renderer throws while constructing a confirmation, review, or preview sheet, catching/retrying the rejected open leaks the previous overlay and its global listeners. Repeated attempts grow DOM memory and make every viewport resize/scroll and Escape key event process more handlers.
Findings.Evidence: buildMobileSheetShell appends the overlay and registers backdrop, window keydown, and visualViewport listeners in shell.disposables. Added line 425 calls renderBody only afterward. The sole normal cleanup path is shell.close(), but a throw skips lines 426-428 and close is never invoked; the Promise constructor only rejects and does not dispose captured resources.
Findings.Recommendation: Wrap the renderer invocation in a cleanup-and-rethrow path that immediately disposes/removes the newly mounted shell (or add an abort method for construction failures), then rethrow so callers still receive the original rejection. Preserve normal ownership by adding a successfully returned body disposable to shell.disposables.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions workbench startup and mobile virtual-keyboard/visual-viewport changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench startup resolves IMobileVisualViewport before renderWorkbench, synchronously binding one context key, registering two browser listeners, and seeding one value. During keyboard or viewport animation, each resize/scroll callback computes one height and publishes observable/CSS/context state; this is on the UI event path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One eager singleton per sessions workbench window; runtime cost scales with visualViewport resize/scroll event frequency, not with a repository or item collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser-event callbacks on the UI thread; one service instance, no queue, IPC, network, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed; unchanged heights are suppressed for the observable, and context-key storage suppresses equal values. The CSS property is written per callback. Cold startup performs one seed update; warm operation reacts only to viewport events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in event frequency and synchronous DOM writes; low confidence that their marginal cost over existing resize layout is material.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CSS style-invalidation cost varies by browser, and the new variable currently has no repository consumer. Existing iOS window code already lays out the workbench on visualViewport resize, so the added publication was not independently strong enough for a performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup work is constant, listeners are singleton-owned and disposed, and the marginal event work does not establish a concrete user-visible slowdown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, search within, select from, and dismiss an existing mobile picker sheet
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening synchronously constructs shell and item-row DOM and focuses a row/input. Dynamic search starts an initial async load and debounces later input by 150 ms; the network/RPC result is not required for the shell to mount but is required before search results appear. Dismissal disposes listeners and cancellation tokens immediately, then removes DOM after 180 ms.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per surfaced remote provider action for the initial empty query and each debounced/drill-down query; typically one in the scoped picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same showMobilePickerSheet search path invoked the same loadItems callback with the same debounce, cancellation, and provider grouping before the shell extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block sheet mounting, but search result population waits for all surfaced-provider requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for each effective non-empty dynamic branch query; the initial empty query reuses branchItems in the inspected caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The picker called the same search source before this PR; the extracted shell does not add, move, or multiply the request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only dynamic branch result refresh waits for the request; sheet mounting and existing static rows do not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Static DOM/listener work scales with visible picker items and returned search results. Search boundary cardinality is one branch-completion RPC per effective query, or one folder-list request per surfaced provider action per effective query; scoped workspace pickers normally surface one provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each new query cancels the prior token and clears the debounce timer. Backend requests can overlap when cancellation cannot abort an already-issued call; folder requests for distinct surfaced providers run concurrently via Promise.all. The PR does not alter this scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The sheet has no result cache. Empty-query population is cold on each open; later queries are debounced and stale results are suppressed by cancellation. Provider connection state may be warm, while remote folder listing and config completion still issue their existing calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged renderResults/loadItems path and traced provider implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Item/result counts and backend latency vary by provider, but their cardinality and scheduling are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: shell construction, viewport adjustment, search request count, cancellation, and close-time disposal are equivalent to the pre-diff picker path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and render the new arbitrary-body mobile content sheet
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper synchronously mounts the shell and invokes renderBody before returning its promise. Normal close disposes shell/body listeners immediately and removes the overlay after 180 ms. A synchronous renderBody failure rejects the promise before any cleanup path runs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Successful construction scales with caller-created body DOM. Failure cost scales without bound with the number of failed/retried opens and with any partial body DOM created before each throw.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Body construction is synchronous. Each leaked failed instance independently remains subscribed to window keydown and visualViewport resize/scroll events, creating event fan-out over time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing. Every call creates a fresh shell; failed calls retain that fresh state indefinitely because no cleanup handle escapes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the mounted shell and listeners are created before the unguarded renderer call, and Promise rejection does not dispose them.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Current repository code does not yet call showMobileContentSheet, so failure prevalence depends on follow-up renderers. The cleanup-loss mechanism is deterministic whenever a renderer throws.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cleanup-lifecycle regression submitted: renderer failure strands mounted DOM and global listeners, causing retained memory and increasing event CPU across retries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install and use the new long-press, pull-down-dismiss, and edge-swipe gesture primitives
Scenarios.CriticalPath: If installed, pointer handlers run synchronously on input events; long press uses one bounded hold timer and click-suppression timer, pull-down updates compositor-oriented transform/opacity styles during drag, and edge swipe performs one geometry read on candidate pointerdown then constant arithmetic on moves.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with installed helper instances and pointer-event frequency. Long-press listeners may scale with rendered rows when future callers attach one per row; pull-down and edge-swipe each track at most one active pointer per installation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per installation, gesture state admits one active pointer. Timers are bounded and reset; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches. State is gesture-local and returned DisposableStore ownership removes listeners/timers. Cold and repeated gestures perform the same constant work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from repository-wide symbol searches showing definitions only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No production caller imports any of the three helpers in this PR, so they add no current product-path event work. Future attachment counts are unknown and cannot establish present regressions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the helpers are currently unreachable from product workflows, and their standalone per-event work is bounded with explicit disposal.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup/viewport input paths, existing picker search boundaries, shell construction/disposal, and all new gesture lifecycles. Submitted one medium cleanup-lifecycle finding for the content-sheet renderer failure path; no other changed mechanism met the evidence threshold.
